contentBlocks.text: This week you learned why and how atoms bond. Let's review it all!

Quick review: atoms bond to achieve a stable octet (Day 1). Ionic bonding transfers electrons, creating charged ions (Day 2). Covalent bonding shares electrons between atoms (Day 3). You learned to predict bond type from metal/nonmetal combinations (Day 4). Predict the bond type for potassium fluoride (potassium, a metal + fluorine, a nonmetal) and for two nitrogen atoms bonding together, and explain both.
Great work this week — you mastered why and how atoms bond, and can predict bond types! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review the octet rule, ionic bonding, covalent bonding, and bond-type prediction
Correctly predict and explain the bond type for potassium fluoride and nitrogen gas
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child predict and explain both new examples.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of chemical-bonding mastery!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often distinguishing ionic vs. covalent) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why two identical nonmetal atoms (like nitrogen) must share rather than transfer electrons
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four chemical-bonding skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: Potassium fluoride is ionic, since potassium is a metal and fluorine is a nonmetal (metal+nonmetal pattern). Two nitrogen atoms bonding together form a covalent bond, since both are the same nonmetal element and neither can transfer an electron away without losing stability — they must share instead.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's NGSS Grade 9-10 chemical-bonding standards (HS-PS1-1/HS-PS1-3) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
